lowest_owning_capability.boundary: public wrapper test isolation and persistent runtime-output hygiene
lowest_owning_capability.reason: The A3 wrapper test writes a fake launcher into the real ignored runtime directory and leaves it there. The accepted daily wrapper then cannot satisfy its rebuild-in-place contract. E1 preserved launcher compatibility but did not originate the contaminating test.
lowest_owning_capability.reopened_claim: The accepted public launcher can be invoked from an ordinarily used worktree after deterministic launcher verification and will rebuild its private runtime binaries in place.

limitations: No real-provider observation occurred, so this artifact establishes no hydration, fence, readiness, committed-time, ranking, T/Q, API/UI, accounting, queue, resource-plateau, heartbeat, or recovery fact.
The authorized 30-minute interval was not consumed as a provider run; the no-retry boundary nevertheless prohibits another attempt without new owner authorization.
